scientific_question: Does a luminosity-weighted foreground-well proxy transfer where raw 2MRS number density did not?
motivation: BHSM/local-topography source strength should track gravitational-well/source strength more closely than unweighted galaxy counts.
primary_weight: K_s-band luminosity proxy proportional to 10^(-0.4 m_K) d_L(z)^2 within each shell
foreground_visibility: only foreground shell path length contributes
controls: same fixed axis, host-mass if available, survey dummies
permutation: redshift-blocked shuffle of the luminosity-weighted foreground score

classification.strong: p<0.01 and sign stable under every leave-one-shell-out test

secondary_transfer: fit one foreground amplitude at 0.01<=z<=0.03 and carry it unchanged to 0.03<z<=0.15
claim_boundary: K_s luminosity is a stellar-mass/gravitational-well proxy, not an SMBH mass measurement
this is a new preregistered hypothesis after failure of the raw-count predictor
no K-band field selection by SN residual performance is allowed; the first valid supported K-band magnitude field is used by fixed priority
